answer:
Automated red teaming can generate diverse test prompts and score failures, but the exercise should target an authorized isolated system with controlled tools and data. Optimize both discovered failure severity and coverage/diversity so the generator does not repeat a single exploit pattern. Use human adjudication to separate actual failures from evaluator errors. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.08073) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.05566)

Partition test discovery from final evaluation to avoid overfitting defenses to the same prompts. Maintain a reproducible corpus, versioned model/tool configurations, and regression checks for repaired cases. Measure false positives and benign-task utility alongside attack success. Reward-model scores are proxies, not proof of safety; adversarially optimizing them can expose weaknesses in the judge instead of the system. Feed verified findings into concrete controls and retest.
